title: Quarterly roadmap: Dedicated capacity governance, autoscale funnel & OKR matrix
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Objective: Create a pragmatic quarterly roadmap that operationalizes Dedicated capacity governance through an 'autoscale funnel' — a set of staged signals, guardrails and playbooks that move workloads from reserve -> warm -> burst while preserving latency SLOs and keeping cost variance predictable.

Scope:
- Define the autoscale funnel taxonomy (Reserve, Prewarm, Burst, Fallback) and the admission signals for each stage (utilization percentiles, queue latency, model memory footprint, KV hit rate).
- Design governance primitives: budgeted warm-pool allocations, per-customer surge allowances, fair-share priority mapping, and rollback policies.
- Produce a quarterly OKR matrix tying each funnel stage to measurable targets (SLOs, fallback rate, cost per 1M tokens, warm-pool utilization efficiency).
- Implement monitoring and dashboards (per-pool and per-customer) plus alert thresholds and on-call runbook updates.
- Define rollout canaries and experiment framework: experiment cohorts, acceptance criteria, rollback criteria.

Deliverables:
1) Autoscale Funnel Spec (Confluence): taxonomy, signals, thresholds, decision tree and APIs for runtime teams. (Draft: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Infra/pages/Autoscale+Funnel+Spec)
2) Governance Playbook: budget cadence, escalation matrix, cost reconciliation process, and SLA breach remediation templates.
3) OKR Matrix & KPIs: a short list of measurable goals for the quarter with owners and dashboards.
4) Dashboard prototypes on Console: warm-pool occupancy, per-customer fallback %, prewarm latency vs. baseline, cost delta. (Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/capacity-autoscale-q1)
5) Runbook and Canary Plan: step-by-step for staged rollout and failure rehearsals.

Success criteria (quarter):
- Fallback rate for dedicated pools <= 4% across top 20 customers under normal load.
- Warm-pool utilization efficiency >= 65% (measured as fraction of reserved tokens redeemed vs. idle capacity).
- 95th percentile tail latency within 1.15x of baseline for canary cohort models.
- No more than 10% month-over-month increase in committed cost for pilot customers unless approved by finance.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Overly aggressive prewarm reduces cost-efficiency. Mitigation: conservative thresholds with A/B experiments and cost budget alarms.
- Risk: Complex governance slows adoption. Mitigation: provide 'starter' policy templates and one-click policy onboarding in Console.
- Risk: SLO regressions during rollout. Mitigation: strict canary acceptance gates and automatic rollback on SLO breach.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Priya Kapoor (owner), Miguel Alvarez (PM lead)
- Engineering: Runtime (lead: Maya Ortiz), Dedicated (lead: Jason Liu)
- Platform & Ops: Oncall owners, Cost Finance (Charlotte Reed)
- Sales/Customer Success: to coordinate pilot customers and communications

Dependencies: ENG-2419 (prefix-based KV cache change), PM-4219 (predictive autoscaler baseline doc), ENG-5023 (console KPI charting primitives).

Notes on scope control: This ticket is explicitly for roadmap definition + OKR mapping and minimal artifacts (spec + playbook + dashboards prototypes). Implementation execution will be split into ENG epics and tracked as sub-issues once the roadmap is approved.
